evals.prompt: Before reviewing this 150% liability cap, make sure you know enough. We have a legal playbook KB and a signed-contracts KB.
evals.expected_output: A minimal retrieval plan that gets current policy from the authoritative playbook and precedent from signed contracts, then stops when the decision is supported.
assertions: The next decision is stated or inferable
The legal playbook is treated as authoritative and contracts as precedent
Retrieval has explicit information objectives
The skill includes a stopping/sufficiency judgment

evals.prompt: Rewrite this paragraph to be shorter. All text is provided. Use know-enough.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes no retrieval is needed because the task is purely transformative and context is sufficient.
assertions: No unnecessary retrieval is proposed
The stopping judgment explains that all evidence needed for the transformation is already present

evals.prompt: Find out whether we have ever offered a similar maintenance concept, and whether the capability is still supported today.
evals.expected_output: The plan separates historical proposal precedent from current product authority and searches both roles.
assertions: Historical precedent and current capability are retrieved from different appropriate source roles
The result does not infer current support from an old proposal alone

evals.prompt: Use know-enough to check whether batch B-12 meets the inspection threshold. All relevant evidence is supplied: the current approved rule QA-4 v3 section 2 requires at least 95% inspected; the complete signed B-12 inspection record dated today reports 98% inspected. Scope and units match, and no conflicting evidence is known. A search service is available.
evals.expected_output: Answers that the supplied record meets the stated threshold, cites both supplied sources, and stops with ENOUGH because further acquisition would not change this bounded check.
assertions: Uses the supplied approved rule and signed record with their references
Does not search merely because a search service is available
Explains sufficiency for this threshold check without claiming broader compliance

evals.prompt: Find the exact inspection interval for reference MX-204 in the accessible current approved maintenance manual. Targeted file reading, exact text search, and semantic search are available. Exact search for MX-204 returns no match; the document index shows the spelling MX 204. The matching section 7.2 states an interval of 90 days.
evals.expected_output: Uses targeted reading or lexical lookup, accounts for the spelling variant, and cites the matching section and current document identity before stopping.
assertions: Prefers direct reading or lexical search over unnecessary semantic retrieval
Does not infer absence from the initial no-match result and checks the relevant spelling variant
Reports the 90-day interval with the original passage and source location
Stops once the exact reference, applicability, and source authority are established

evals.prompt: Which active test facilities in region West support loads of at least 20 tonnes? An authorized structured-query capability exposes the current facility register and its dictionary; a document search capability is also available. The schema has facility_id, status, region, and max_load_kg. The dictionary defines 1 tonne as 1000 kg and status A as active. Rows are F-1/A/West/25000, F-2/A/West/15000, F-3/I/West/30000, F-4/A/East/25000.
evals.expected_output: Selects structured querying, resolves schema and units, filters status A, region West, and max_load_kg >= 20000, and returns only F-1 with traceable query logic and records.
assertions: Requests a structured capability that the environment actually provides
Checks the schema, category definitions, units, and facility identifiers
Returns F-1 only, with reproducible filters and record provenance
Does not add semantic search or specialized classification when the exact query suffices

evals.prompt: Why are teams informally bypassing design review? Evaluate this prompt separately in two fictional environments with the same know-enough instructions. Environment A offers tools called Lantern and Folio; environment B offers tools called Pebble and Ledger. In each environment, the first tool searches accessible approved procedures and incident narratives with lexical, semantic, or hybrid retrieval and returns document IDs, dates, locations, and scores; the second reads original passages. The environments expose equivalent sources and evidence: current procedure P-2 section 4 requires review, incident I-7 paragraph 3 reports a queue delay, and incident I-8 paragraph 2 reports duplicate data entry. Incident authors use 'skip the gate' rather than 'bypass design review'. There is no structured database or specialized classifier.
evals.expected_output: In each environment, requests appropriate conceptual or text retrieval, checks original passages, distinguishes current policy from reported workarounds, and offers a bounded explanation supported by the incidents. The harness maps the strategy to the tools actually exposed without changing the skill.
assertions: Both runs apply the same functional strategy and evidence requirements despite renamed tools
Uses text, semantic, or hybrid retrieval appropriate to vocabulary variation without requiring a structured-first sequence
Inspects and cites original passages and keeps normative procedure distinct from incident observations
Does not treat similarity scores as authority or impose a universal threshold
Works without a specialized classifier and stops with explicit limits on the explanatory coverage

evals.prompt: Find active facilities with capacity >= 20 tonnes that have handled a similar salt-fog endurance test. Authorized structured querying, documentary search, source reading, and established-relationship lookup are available. The current register qualifies F-1 and F-2. Historical reports T-9 and T-11 describe relevant tests and link to F-1 through stable facility_id; report T-10 describes a different procedure and mentions a site name resembling F-2 but has no verified facility link.
evals.expected_output: Uses a minimal composite plan to establish current eligibility, find relevant historical passages, and verify facility links. Reports supported experience for F-1 while marking F-2's experience unsupported by the available evidence.
assertions: States the knowledge objective, requested capabilities, accessible sources, expected evidence per step, and stopping criterion in ordinary language
Combines structured and documentary evidence only to meet the two material requirements
Reconciles records and passages using stable IDs and attested relationships rather than similar names
Keeps current eligibility separate from historical experience and preserves provenance across steps
Does not infer truth from a successful join or claim F-2 has never performed such a test
Accepts an evidence-justified order without requiring structured search before documentary retrieval

evals.prompt: Determine what evidence is needed to compare approved welding procedures for thin aluminium. Accessible manuals can be read and searched by exact terms or concepts. Evaluate three independent variants: (A) no specialized classifier is installed; (B) an authorized optional classifier fails; (C) it returns an ambiguous routing judgment. The active model and the reading/search capabilities remain available in every variant.
evals.expected_output: In every variant, reasons about the material gap using rules or the active model, selects a minimal available search strategy, and judges sufficiency from consulted source evidence.
assertions: Treats missing classification as normal and continues after failure or ambiguity without requiring installation
The active model remains responsible for the fallback strategy
Does not invent a service, endpoint, or classification result
Bases sufficiency on original source evidence rather than classification confidence

evals.prompt: What is the current approved retention period for project records? Evaluate three independent environments. (A) A registry names the policy repository, but access is denied; the only readable source is an old draft. (B) The source is authorized, but the harness has no way to search or read it. (C) Authorized search and reading work, but targeted reference and spelling-variant searches return no applicable policy. No further authoritative source is available in any variant.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes denied access, missing capability, and a genuine no-match result. Explains why the current requirement is NOT ENOUGH supported, reports the specific missing authoritative evidence and limits, and stops without fabricating a period.
assertions: Does not claim a denied or technically unreadable source was searched
Does not treat a registry entry as access authorization or an old draft as current authority
Distinguishes no match from source inaccessibility and does not infer that no retention rule exists
Does not invent tools, data, or a current requirement and does not create a new tool by default
Reports NOT ENOUGH, the missing evidence, and whether the task can safely proceed instead of looping

evals.prompt: What inspection interval applies to pump class P? Two accessible approved bulletins cover class P: B-7 v2 section 3 says 30 days; B-8 v1 section 5 says 60 days. Their effective dates overlap, neither declares supersession, and search gives B-8 a higher similarity score. A bounded check of their approval metadata and scope reveals no rule resolving the conflict.
evals.expected_output: Cites both bulletins, identifies the unresolved material conflict, checks authority/dates/scope proportionately, and returns NOT ENOUGH for a definitive interval with the unresolved authority question explicit.
assertions: Preserves both conflicting source claims and locations
Does not silently choose the higher score, average the intervals, or invent a supersession rule
Limits further retrieval to evidence that could resolve the conflict
Reports the remaining uncertainty and NOT ENOUGH when accessible checks cannot settle the requirement

evals.prompt: Find requirement R-9 in an accessible approved scanned inspection report. The current tools cannot read its image text. The harness exposes a document-preparation capability. Evaluate two variants: (A) preparation would upload the report to an external service, and that transfer has no authorization; (B) local preparation is already explicitly authorized and yields R-9 on page 6 with the original document identity preserved, but the extracted wording is partly illegible.
evals.expected_output: In A, explains the preparation and transfer scope needed and does not ingest or upload without authorization. In B, delegates within existing authorization, preserves provenance, and reports insufficient evidence for the illegible requirement unless a targeted source check can resolve it.
assertions: Distinguishes source access from authorization to prepare or transmit content
Does not automatically ingest or upload in variant A or install an ingestion engine
Uses the available authorized capability in variant B without requesting the same permission again
Retains the source identity and page location after preparation
Does not treat successful extraction as proof of a complete or accurate requirement; reports the remaining evidence gap
